body:
What is biotechnology?

Biotechnology is the application of living organisms, their cells, enzymes or biological components to develop useful products, processes and services. It connects biological knowledge with practical needs in medicine, agriculture, industry and environmental protection.

Biotechnology is not limited to genetic engineering. Humans have used microorganisms for centuries to make curd, bread and fermented products. Modern biotechnology extends these applications through improved biological processes, genetic information, cell culture and recombinant DNA technology.

Genetic engineering deliberately alters genetic material to obtain a desired characteristic. Genomics studies the complete genetic information of an organism. Fermentation uses the metabolic activity of microorganisms to produce useful substances. All 3 are associated with biotechnology, but they are not the same process.

Basic biological terms

DNA is the hereditary material of most organisms. A gene is a functional segment of DNA that contributes to the production of a functional RNA or protein. A genome is the complete genetic material of an organism. Genome sequencing determines the order of DNA bases, while bioinformatics uses computational methods to analyse biological information.

Reading a genome does not itself change that genome. For example, sequencing a pathogen can help researchers identify genetic variations, whereas genetic engineering changes genetic material to obtain a particular characteristic or product.

The 4 major biotechnology sectors

Gujarat's Biotechnology Policy 2022–27 uses the broad national classification of biotechnology into biopharma, bio-agriculture, bio-industrial and bio-services. The distinction is based mainly on the application or service being provided.

SectorMain activityExamples
BiopharmaDeveloping healthcare products using biological processesVaccines, recombinant proteins, biological medicines
Bio-agricultureImproving crops and agricultural inputsBt cotton, biofertilisers, tissue-cultured plants
Bio-industrialUsing biological processes in manufacturingIndustrial enzymes, fermentation products, biofuels
Bio-servicesProviding biological research, analysis and technical servicesGenomics, bioinformatics, molecular diagnostics, contract research

Why Gujarat has a biotechnology ecosystem

Gujarat has an established base in pharmaceuticals, chemicals and industrial manufacturing. Biotechnology can build upon this base through research institutions, specialised industrial facilities, trained personnel and companies that develop products from biological systems.

For example, a research centre may identify a useful microbial strain, an incubator may help a start-up develop a product, and a manufacturer may produce it at commercial scale. Government policy can support these activities, while the applicable regulatory authority examines safety and legal compliance.

These functions are related, but they are not interchangeable. An organisation that promotes biotechnology does not automatically have the authority to approve a vaccine or permit environmental release of a genetically modified crop.

Biotechnology is broader than genetic modification. A product made using an ordinary yeast strain can be a biotechnology product even when the yeast has not been genetically modified. Conversely, a pharmaceutical product made entirely through conventional chemical synthesis is not automatically a biotechnology product.

Prelims focus

  • Biotechnology uses living systems or biological components to create useful products and services.
  • Genomics studies genetic information; genetic engineering alters genetic material.
  • The 4 broad sectors are biopharma, bio-agriculture, bio-industrial and bio-services.
  • Fermentation is an example of biotechnology that does not necessarily involve genetic modification.
  • Trap: Biotechnology and genetic engineering are not synonyms.

[NCERT, Biology, Class 12, chapter 11, Biotechnology: Principles and Processes, pp. 218–220; NCERT, Science, Class 8, chapter 2, Microorganisms: Friend and Foe, pp. 17–21; Government of Gujarat, Gujarat State Biotechnology (BT) Policy 2022–27, sections 2 and 5, pp. 1 and 5–6, dated 15 February 2022.]

title: Biotechnology and the Gujarat Economy: Meaning, Foundations and Major Sectors

body:
Why different institutions are needed

A biotechnology sector requires more than factories. Researchers investigate biological problems, universities prepare skilled personnel, incubators support new enterprises, industrial parks provide infrastructure, and government agencies frame development policies.

Gujarat has established specialised institutions to perform these different functions. Their full names, locations and roles are important because similar abbreviations can easily be confused.

Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission

The Gujarat State Biotechnology Mission (GSBTM) was established in 2004 under the Government of Gujarat's Department of Science and Technology. It is the state's nodal agency for promoting biotechnology development.

Its work includes supporting research, encouraging biotechnology education and skill development, promoting entrepreneurship and helping formulate development measures. GSBTM is primarily a promotion and coordination institution, not a national authority for approving medicines or genetically modified crops.

Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre

The Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre (GBRC) is an autonomous research organisation under the state's Department of Science and Technology. It was established in 2017, with commencement on 1 September 2017, and is based in Gandhinagar.

Its major areas include genomics and bioinformatics. Research applications extend to healthcare, agriculture, industrial biotechnology, environmental studies and marine biotechnology. The centre also provides shared laboratory infrastructure for researchers, students, start-ups and industry.

A research centre may study the genetic variation of a disease-causing microorganism or examine a biological problem affecting agriculture. Such research can guide future applications, but a research finding is not automatically an approved commercial product.

Gujarat Biotechnology University

Gujarat Biotechnology University (GBU) was established through the Gujarat Biotechnology University Act, 2018, identified as Gujarat Act 16 of 2018. Its headquarters are specified at GIFT City, Gandhinagar.

The university provides advanced education and research opportunities in areas such as medical, industrial, plant, animal and environmental biotechnology. Its academic collaboration with the University of Edinburgh is a distinctive institutional feature.

The main distinction is that GBU is an educational and research university, while GBRC is a specialised state biotechnology research centre. Both can conduct research, but their institutional identities and principal functions differ.

Savli Technology and Business Incubator

The Savli Technology and Business Incubator (STBI) is located in the Savli GIDC Industrial Estate at Manjusar, Vadodara. It supports entrepreneurs and technology-based start-ups by providing facilities such as shared laboratories, equipment, working space and mentoring.

An incubator helps an early-stage enterprise develop and test its idea. Its purpose is not simply to provide land for a large factory. Although STBI initially focused on biotechnology and life sciences, its stated entrepreneurial support is not restricted exclusively to biotechnology.

Savli Biotechnology Park

The Savli Biotechnology Park is an industrial biotechnology initiative associated with GSBTM and the Gujarat Industrial Development Corporation (GIDC) in the Savli area near Vadodara.

The GSBTM project description envisaged a biotechnology park of approximately 700 acres in 3 phases, intended to support biotechnology-related industrial and research activity. This figure describes the project's announced plan. It should not be interpreted as independently verified completed development or occupied industrial land as of 13 November 2026.

The park and STBI are geographically associated but conceptually distinct. A biotechnology park concerns a wider industrial development area, whereas an incubator provides direct facilities and guidance to developing enterprises.

InstitutionLocationPrimary identity
GSBTMGandhinagarState biotechnology promotion and coordination
GBRCGandhinagarSpecialised biotechnology research
GBUGIFT City, GandhinagarUniversity education and research
STBISavli, VadodaraTechnology and start-up incubation
Savli Biotechnology ParkSavli, VadodaraBiotechnology industrial development initiative

Prelims focus

  • GSBTM was established in 2004 under Gujarat's Department of Science and Technology.
  • GBRC was established in 2017 and is associated with genomics and bioinformatics research.
  • GBU was established under Gujarat Act 16 of 2018 and is associated with GIFT City, Gandhinagar.
  • STBI is located at Savli, Manjusar, Vadodara.
  • The Savli Biotechnology Park project is associated with GSBTM and GIDC.
  • Trap: An incubator, a university, a research centre and an industrial park are different kinds of institutions.

[Government of Gujarat, Gujarat State Biotechnology (BT) Policy 2022–27, sections 3.1 and 6, pp. 3 and 10; Gujarat Department of Science and Technology, Gujarat Biotechnology Research Centre, Overview and establishment details; Gujarat Department of Science and Technology, Gujarat Biotechnology University, Overview and Gujarat Act 16 of 2018; Gujarat Government notification dated 20 November 2023 specifying GBU headquarters; Savli Technology and Business Incubator, Introduction and Facilities; GSBTM, Biotech Park: Savli, Vadodara, Prelude and Envisaged Project Contours; official websites consulted 13 November 2026.]

body:
Pharmaceutical manufacturing and biotechnology

The pharmaceutical industry develops and manufactures medicines. Some medicines are made mainly through chemical synthesis, while others are produced using living cells or biological processes. The second group forms an important part of biopharmaceutical manufacturing.

Gujarat's established pharmaceutical and chemical industries provide industrial experience and infrastructure that can also support biological medicines, vaccines and biotechnology services. However, the entire pharmaceutical industry should not be classified as biotechnology.

Active ingredients and finished medicines

An active pharmaceutical ingredient (API) is the substance responsible for a medicine's intended pharmacological action. A formulation is the finished medicine in a suitable form, such as a tablet, capsule or injection, containing the active ingredient and other necessary components.

For example, a manufacturer may produce an API at one facility and use it in a tablet or injectable product at another. API manufacturing and finished-dosage manufacturing are related stages, not identical activities.

The source of the active ingredient also matters. An API can be chemically synthesised or biologically derived. The word API does not, by itself, mean that genetic engineering was used.

Small-molecule medicines and biological medicines

FeatureConventional small-molecule medicineBiological medicine
Usual productionChemical synthesisBiological systems or living cells
Typical structureRelatively small and well-defined moleculeOften a larger, more complex biological substance
ExampleParacetamolRecombinant human insulin
Related follow-on productGeneric medicineBiosimilar medicine

A generic medicine contains the same active ingredient as the reference medicine and must meet applicable quality and equivalence requirements. A biosimilar is a biological medicine demonstrated to be highly similar to an approved reference biological medicine, without clinically meaningful differences under the applicable regulatory standards.

Biological medicines can be complex because they are produced through biological systems. For that reason, biosimilars are assessed through a comparison appropriate to biological products rather than treated as simple chemical copies.

Recombinant human insulin as an example

Insulin is a hormone that helps regulate blood glucose. Earlier medicinal insulin was obtained from animal sources. Recombinant DNA technology made it possible to produce human insulin through genetically engineered microorganisms.

The central principle is that the genetic information needed to produce human insulin can be introduced into a suitable production system. The resulting protein is then processed into a medicinal product. This illustrates how genetic engineering can contribute to the manufacture of a therapeutic substance.

Not every biological medicine is a vaccine. Insulin is used to treat diabetes, whereas a vaccine is designed to prepare the immune system against a particular disease. Both can involve biotechnology, but they serve different purposes.

Gujarat's manufacturing connection

Zydus Lifesciences, historically associated with the name Zydus Cadila, provides a documented example of Gujarat's pharmaceutical and biotechnology activities. Its 2021–22 annual report identified vaccine manufacturing facilities at Changodar and Moraiya in the Ahmedabad region, including facilities associated with ZyCoV-D and rabies vaccines.

The same report identified API manufacturing facilities at Ankleshwar, among other locations. These are documented company facilities for the 2021–22 reporting period; the report alone should not be used to establish the precise present-day operating status of each production line in November 2026.

These examples show the relationship between Gujarat's pharmaceutical manufacturing base and biotechnology. They do not mean that all products made at these locations are genetically engineered.

Why quality control matters

Medicines must have appropriate identity, purity, strength and quality. Manufacturing therefore includes controlled production, examination of product quality, suitable packaging and storage. These requirements are particularly important for products whose biological activity may be affected by unsuitable conditions.

Specialised biological products may also require controlled temperatures during storage and transport. A cold chain is a temperature-controlled system used to protect products that require such conditions; it is not a universal requirement that every medicine must be refrigerated.

Prelims focus

  • API means active pharmaceutical ingredient; a formulation is the finished medicine.
  • Recombinant human insulin is an example of a biological medicine.
  • Generic medicines and biosimilars are not identical regulatory concepts.
  • Zydus Lifesciences documented vaccine facilities at Changodar and Moraiya in its 2021–22 annual report.
  • The same annual report documented API manufacturing at Ankleshwar.
  • Trap: All pharmaceutical manufacturing is not necessarily biotechnology.

[NCERT, Biology, Class 12, chapter 12, Biotechnology and Its Applications, section 12.2.1, pp. 235–236; Zydus Lifesciences Limited, Annual Report 2021–22, Corporate Information: Manufacturing Facilities and Research Centres; Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, Functions, official website consulted 13 November 2026.]
